title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
main_claim: Every elliptic curve E over an imaginary quadratic field K is modular, with matching local parameters at every place and L(E/K,s)=L(pi_E,s-1/2). For non-CM E the proof picks p>100 with SL2 mod-p image and sets n=3p, F=K(mu_n). It builds a genus-n cyclic cover C_n(t) of a quadratic twist B_t of E, branched at two points, and uses rank-two rotation-character pieces V_eta=H^1(A_t), V_chi, V_psi, V_1=H^1(B_t). These satisfy the congruences eta≡chi mod p, chi≡psi mod 3 and psi≡1 mod p, which come from freeness of H^1 over Z[mu_n]. The starting point is Caraiani–Newton Thm 6.1 at the prime 5. Automorphy is then lifted three times with CN Thm 5.2. A compact-type E^n degeneration plus local constancy prescribes the local types at 3p. Two explicit transvections with off-diagonal entry 2-u-u^{-1}, plus Hilbert irreducibility over Res_{K/Q}U, give residual irreducibility and decomposed genericity. The result then descends from F to K by cyclic base change. The CM case is handled separately by CM theory.

issues.description: The supplementary claim that the local factors also match when the Weil–Deligne representation is taken at the residue-characteristic coefficient prime is only sketched. One example is that inertia nontriviality is said to follow from the crystalline good-reduction criterion. This claim is not needed for the main theorem, which is proved using a coefficient prime different from the residue characteristic.
issues.evidence: 'At the residue-characteristic coefficient prime, nontriviality of inertia follows from the crystalline good-reduction criterion [ColemanIovita]' — stated without the p-adic WD construction details. The main theorem's local statement is for v∤l and comes from CN Lemma 6.1.3(3).

coverage:
I read every section: geometry, monodromy, systems, automorphy inputs, local, residual, automorphy and descent. Checks done:
- Geometry: the divisor sum and principality; f(-Z)=1/f(Z); the genus via Riemann–Hurwitz and Chevalley–Weil; f_exc(0)=1 for odd n; the compact-type tree giving E^m; the order-m class -a/m at the second fiber; node smoothing order one.
- Monodromy: the vanishing classes a_i-a_{i+1} and the Picard–Lefschetz sum giving 2a_j-a_{j±1}.
- Character pieces: the Z[mu]^2 freeness and the evaluation-congruence lemma; the determinant via the alternating pairing <x,w*y>; Hodge numbers a_theta=1; genus of D_t=C_3/w equal to 1.
- Residual: the traces 2+στk c^2 for c=3, k=2 (20 and -16, which avoid ±2 mod 5 and mod p>100); the degree-≤4 argument for the (p,3) pair; the trace-±2 count in SL2(F_p); the joint-image bound 4p/(p^2-1).
- Specialization: the Res_{K/Q} Hilbert irreducibility and Chebotarev conjugation argument; local constancy of toric rank and Newton polygon via d-adic torsion; the ordinary, supersingular and toric conclusions for each character summand; the zero-monodromy and Steinberg arguments via Varma.
- Descent: cyclic base change with the character twist.
- Citations: I downloaded CN arXiv v3 and compared Thm 5.2, Def 2.1.27, Remark 5.2.2, Thm 6.1 and Lemma 6.1.3 verbatim. The paper's specialized statements are implied by them; for example, CN (5)(b)/(c) match alternatives (i)/(ii).
Not independently verified: the deep inputs themselves (CN, HLTT/Scholze, Varma, base change).
